text:
Brandon Hagel scored twice in 21 seconds late in the third period, and the second of those goals was the one that broke a tie game open. The first came on a 3% chance, a wrist shot from a spot where almost nothing goes in, at 18:16. At 18:37 he added a snap shot (49% to score) for the 5-3 final, and he finished with three goals and an assist.

The scoreboard made TBL look like the clear winner, but the play said otherwise. TBL deserved to win 51% of the time and NYI 49%, a coin flip. Expected goals were 3.06 for TBL and 2.51 for NYI, but at even strength NYI held the edge, 1.45 to 1.26. The second period tilted toward the home side, 1.75 to 1.38, and that's where NYI erased a 3-1 deficit. Tony DeAngelo and Jean-Gabriel Pageau scored at even strength, and Brayden Schenn tipped in a power-play goal at 19:53 to tie it at 3-3. That one was a 67% chance.

Jake Guentzel opened the scoring and added a power-play goal in the second, so TBL got two goals from him and the three from Hagel. Ilya Sorokin allowed 1.4 goals more than the 25 shots against him deserved, while Andrei Vasilevskiy was about half a goal short of expectation. NYI delivered 30 hits to TBL's 18 and took 13 penalty minutes to 9. The tie held until the final three minutes, and TBL took what a game with even chances handed it.
